edges.description: The untransduced patient line reproduces the disease's biochemical signature: reduced oxygen consumption and reduced activity of the mtDNA-dependent complexes, with complex II, which is entirely nuclear encoded, unaffected.
edges.limitations: The complex profile is not the one the muscle shows. Patient muscle enzymology gives a combined complex I and IV deficiency, which is what this disease is named for; the fibroblasts have complexes I, III and IV reduced. Fibroblasts are also not a tissue this disease damages, so the model reports the ubiquitous biochemical lesion and says nothing about why the damage falls on cochlea, brain and beta cell.

edges.description: Lentiviral wild-type NARS2 restores respiration and complex I, III and IV activity in the patient line, and the DFNB94 allele p.Val213Phe does not. The paired arms establish that the biochemical deficit follows from the NARS2 lesion, and grade p.Val213Phe as functionally deficient.
edges.limitations: Rescue is incomplete and the authors say so, offering several candidate reasons including a heteroplasmic mt-tRNA-Cys variant they found in the same patient. Overexpression from a lentiviral construct is also not restoration of endogenous dosage, so the arm shows that supplying functional NARS2 helps, not that the deficit is quantitatively explained by the amount of NARS2 lost.

edges.limitations: What this model measures is the size of the mt-tRNA-Asn pool, not the fraction of it that is charged. The same paper measured the charged to uncharged ratio in the same cells and found it normal, so the node's claim that less charged tRNA-Asn reaches the ribosome rests on the reduced pool here plus the directly reduced charged fraction that the founding family's lymphoblasts show, and not on this measurement alone. High passage number also prevented the measurement in the second proband, so n is one patient.

nodes.description:
The severe pole of the disease, and the presentation the founding Leigh syndrome family defines. Early-onset NARS2 encephalopathy takes an Alpers or Leigh shape, with bilateral symmetric brainstem and thalamic lesions in the Leigh cases, a more severe course and poorer survival than the other NARS2 presentations.
The binding is deliberately the generic HP:0002448 Progressive encephalopathy rather than a Leigh-specific term. HPO has no Leigh syndrome phenotype term, and the two narrower candidates are both wrong here: HP:0006976 Necrotizing encephalopathy would assert the Leigh lesion pattern in patients the source describes only as sharing features of Alpers *or* Leigh syndrome, and Alpers is not a necrotizing encephalopathy. HP:0002415, which the deep-research report offers for Leigh syndrome, is Leukodystrophy.

nodes.description: The step from a ubiquitous biochemical defect to a tissue-restricted clinical picture, and the one this disease does not explain. A synthetase expressed in every cell produces disease concentrated in cochlea, brain and the pancreatic beta cell, and the founding literature names that tissue specificity as unexpected and unexplained. The node is therefore coarse on purpose and its outgoing edges carry no claimed intermediates.

nodes.description: The only model system in this disease that does more than describe it. It has two arms, and the second is what makes it worth recording: re-expressing wild-type NARS2 in the patient's own fibroblasts raises oxygen consumption and complex I, III and IV activity, while re-expressing the hearing-loss allele p.Val213Phe in the same cells does not. That pairing is what converts a correlation between genotype and biochemistry into a causal claim, and it simultaneously grades the DFNB94 allele as pathogenic in a system where no DFNB94 patient tissue is available.

nodes.description: Biallelic NARS2 variants reduce or abolish mitochondrial asparaginyl-tRNA synthetase. The reported mechanisms differ by allele and are not all the same: the founding c.822G>C change disrupts the 3' splice site of exon 7 and removes exon 7 and part of exon 8 from the transcript; p.Tyr323* yields no detectable protein; p.Asn381Ser lowers protein level and disrupts dimerisation; and p.Val213Phe, the hearing-loss allele, leaves oligomerisation intact.

nodes.description: Less aminoacylated mt-tRNA-Asn available to the mitochondrial ribosome. This is the step that makes the disease a translation disorder rather than an enzyme-deficiency disorder in the usual metabolic sense: nothing accumulates upstream and no substrate is diverted, the ribosome simply stalls more often.
